**Fix: casting to a browser no longer plays only sound.** Some streams carry HEVC video in TS segments, which Safari's own player can't show, so casting to Safari (or a TV browser) gave sound with no picture.

- The page now switches to its own player automatically and carries on from the same spot.
- If a browser still can't show the picture, the page and your phone say so, with the video's format.

The browser or TV needs internet access for the switch.

versions.notes:
**Fix: casting to a browser no longer plays only sound.** Some streams carry HEVC video in TS segments, which Safari's own player can't show, so casting to Safari (or a TV browser) gave sound with no picture.

- The page now switches to its own player automatically and carries on from the same spot.
- If a browser still can't show the picture, the page and your phone say so, with the video's format.

The browser or TV needs internet access for the switch.

**One Cast button.** The player used to have three buttons for putting the video on a TV. It now has one, **Cast to TV**.

- It opens a single sheet that lists the Google Cast and DLNA TVs on your Wi-Fi together. Tap one to connect.
- Below the list: **Screen mirroring…** opens your phone's own cast screen for Miracast TVs, and **TV not listed?** shows an address to open in your TV's browser.
- While you are casting, the sheet says who you are casting to and has a Stop button.

Phone and TV need to be on the same Wi-Fi.

**Play on TV, without extra hardware.** For TVs that Google Cast and Miracast don't reach, the player has a new Play on TV button.

- It lists the DLNA TVs on your Wi-Fi. Tap one and the video plays there while your phone keeps the controls.
- TV not listed? The same sheet shows a short address to open in your TV's own browser, and the video plays there. Pausing or stopping hands the position back to your phone.
- If a TV refuses a stream, the player says so and points you to the browser option.

Phone and TV need to be on the same Wi-Fi.

**Fixes and polish:** watch progress is now kept per season (episode 1 of season 2 no longer overwrites episode 1 of season 1). Settings is simpler: five clear sections and a "Show advanced settings" switch. The player is easier to use on a phone: a roomier title, one More menu, a clean failed-playback screen, a seek bar that screen readers can use. Search says so when the network failed instead of "No results", episodes get a Try Again button, poster grids fill the screen evenly, text is easier to read, and error messages are in plain words.

**Fix:** shows whose portal lists a season in pages now show every episode. Some portals send 14 at a time, newest first, so the oldest episodes (like Season 1 Episode 1) were missing; the same applies to shows with many seasons.

**Arc TV for Android** 0.1.8 (early access). Phones and tablets, Android 8.0 or newer.

**What's new:** the app can now update itself. Open **Settings → Updates** to check, download and install new versions, and
Arc TV looks for updates when it opens (you can turn that off). Also in this build: the floating glass tab bar, portal
export, Miracast, per-season downloads, live channels in Search, and a Series tab with its own categories.
